en.title: A One-Day Puncak Itinerary from Bogor, with a Driver
en.metaTitle: One-Day Puncak Itinerary from Bogor — Arasya Blog
en.metaDescription: A day in Puncak from Bogor: when to leave to beat the one-way system, the destinations in the right order, and the costs to budget for.
en.excerpt: A day in Puncak from Bogor — the right departure time, the destinations in one direction, and the costs to have ready.

sections.heading: Leave before the one-way system starts
paragraphs: On weekends and public holidays the police run a one-way system on the Puncak road: uphill traffic gets priority in the morning, downhill in the afternoon. The timings shift with the day's volume, so leaving an hour later can cost you two or three hours on the road.

We suggest a pickup between 05.30 and 06.00 from Bogor. As well as clearing the climb before it fills, you reach the tea plantations while the morning mist is still down — the best light of the day for photographs.

sections.heading: Visit them in one direction
paragraphs: The whole trick to a Puncak day is moving steadily uphill without doubling back: start at Taman Safari Indonesia in Cisarua, carry on to the tea plantations for a walk between the rows, then Atta'awun Mosque at the highest point of the road.

The descent leaves room for an early dinner and souvenirs around Cimory, or an alternative route through Sentul if the downhill direction has not opened yet — a call best left to the driver, who is watching the day's conditions.
list: Taman Safari Indonesia — open from early morning, allow about 3 hours
Puncak tea plantations — an easy walk and photographs among the rows
Atta'awun Mosque — a rest and prayers at the highest point of the road
Cimory Riverside — an early dinner and souvenirs before the descent

sections.heading: What to budget for
paragraphs: On the All-in rate the fare already covers fuel, tolls, and the driver's meals — you only need entry tickets and parking. On the In-City 12-hour rate those are counted separately; both are itemised in the rate table on the Bogor page.
For a family group, one MPV with a driver almost always works out cheaper than two small cars you drive yourselves — and it spares you the climb.

en.title: Chasing Sunrise at Borobudur from Yogyakarta
en.metaTitle: Borobudur Sunrise from Yogyakarta: Timing & Quotas — Arasya Blog
en.metaDescription: Leaving Yogyakarta before dawn for Borobudur: where to watch the sunrise, how the temple-climb quota works, and a route home that keeps the day whole.
en.excerpt: Leaving Jogja before dawn — where to watch the sunrise, how the temple-climb quota works, and how to plan the way back so the day stays yours.

sections.heading: What time do you need to leave Jogja?
paragraphs: Yogyakarta to Borobudur is about 40 kilometres, or 1 to 1.5 hours. For a sunrise around 05.30 the ideal pickup is 03.30 — enough for the drive, collecting tickets, and the walk to the viewpoint.
Leaving that early also means empty roads; our drivers usually take the Jalan Godean–Kalibawang route, which is shorter than the main Magelang road.

sections.heading: Sunrise from the temple, or from the hill?
paragraphs: Watching dawn from Borobudur's upper terraces needs a special package with a limited quota, best booked well in advance. Punthuk Setumbu is the alternative: the silhouette of Borobudur under a blanket of mist, seen from a distance, for a far smaller ticket price.
If the temple quota has gone you can still go up after regular opening — pair Setumbu for the dawn with Borobudur straight afterwards.

sections.heading: Planning the way back
paragraphs: By nine in the morning the main event is over — far too early to head home. The sequence we recommend: Bukit Rhema's Chicken Church, breakfast beside the Progo river, then Pawon and Mendut temples, which sit on the same axis.
Coming back into Jogja through Sleman, you still have the afternoon for Malioboro or for doing nothing at all — a full day, without any of it rushed.
list: Book the temple sunrise quota several days ahead
Bring a jacket — it is 17–20°C before dawn
A phone torch is enough for the Punthuk Setumbu path
Eat after sunrise — the local warungs open around 07.00

en.title: BTS, Taxi, or a Car with a Driver? Weighing Up Family Transport in Bangkok
en.metaTitle: Family Transport in Bangkok: BTS, Taxi or Driver? — Arasya Blog
en.metaDescription: An honest comparison of getting around Bangkok as a family: when the BTS and MRT win, when a taxi is enough, and when a car with a driver makes sense.
en.excerpt: An honest comparison of getting around Bangkok as a family — when public transport wins, and when a car with a driver is the sensible choice.

sections.heading: BTS and MRT: fast, but only so far
paragraphs: Bangkok's rail network is reliable and immune to traffic, but it only covers the central corridors. The Grand Palace, the floating markets, and Ayutthaya — the things most visitors came for — are not practically reachable by rail.
For a family travelling with children or older relatives, changing lines by staircase and standing in a packed carriage at rush hour drains a day quickly.

sections.heading: Taxis and ride-hailing: fine over short distances
paragraphs: Metered taxis and ride-hailing apps make sense for short hops between districts. The difficulty is on longer trips: communicating in Thai, a meter that keeps running through the jams, and not enough boot space for a group.
Out of the city the fares climb and become hard to predict — the spending gets away from you in a way a daily hire does not.

sections.heading: When a car with a driver is the sensible choice
paragraphs: For four people or more with a schedule that crosses districts — and certainly for a day out to Damnoen Saduak, Ayutthaya, or Pattaya — one car with a driver for the day buys certainty over both cost and time.

With Arasya the coordination runs through our admin team in Indonesian or English: you tell us the plan, we set the route and the hotel pickup times — and nobody has to negotiate anything at the roadside.
list: Short hops, or late at night → metered taxi or an app
A family of 4+, or leaving the city → a car with a driver
Airport to hotel: a scheduled pickup beats the taxi queue
